item.title: Signature Optional - Analysis of CVE-2026-28323
item.description:
CVE-2026-28323 in SolarWinds Web Help Desk allows full session takeover via a single forged SAML POST, no credentials required. Bishop Fox confirmed end-to-end exploitation.
Key findings:
- SolarWinds Web Help Desk treated SAML signature verification as optional and skipped all remaining spec-required validation steps, meaning an attacker could forge an arbitrary SAML assertion and the application accepted it as legitimate.
- Bishop Fox confirmed the full exploit chain end to end: one crafted POST request with a forged SAML response, zero credentials, full authenticated session returned. No chained CVEs, no prior foothold needed. Exploitation is trivially reproducible.
- DFIR artifact focus: hunt your web server access logs for POST requests to the SAML assertion consumer service endpoint with malformed or unsigned SAMLResponse values, especially those resulting in HTTP 200 or redirect responses that indicate session creation.
- Scope: any SolarWinds Web Help Desk deployment with SAML SSO enabled is affected until the patch is applied. Web Help Desk is common in enterprise IT and MSP environments, making this a high-value lateral movement or initial access target.
Patch immediately. If patching is delayed, disable SAML SSO and fall back to local authentication. Review auth logs for unexpected SSO-authenticated sessions, particularly service or admin accounts. Full technical root cause and detection detail are in the Bishop Fox report.

item.title: Incident response guide for AWS CloudTrail investigations – Part 1
item.description:
AWS CloudTrail investigation playbook from AWS SIRT breaks down two real incident scenarios: cross-account S3 ransomware-style deletion and console-credential cryptomining via CloudFormation, with annotated log evidence throughout.
Key findings:
- In Scenario 1, a threat actor assumed the CrossAccountS3Access role from a trusted account, used a masquerading session name "dev-migration-script" to blend into operational noise, performed ListBuckets recon at 14:31:22Z, then executed scripted REST.COPY.OBJECT exfiltration followed by REST.DELETE.OBJECT destruction of q4-2024.xlsx, pii-database.csv, and prod-database-backup.sql within a 13-second window. The copy-then-delete sequence is the ransomware tell: data was stolen before destruction to enable extortion.
- In Scenario 2, console credentials without MFA (mfaAuthenticated: false) let a threat actor deploy a CloudFormation stack named CRYPTO in us-east-1 just 50 seconds after session creation. The userAgent field (exec-env/CloudShell) reveals they launched CloudShell to run a prepackaged script, bypassing static API key monitoring while staying inside the console trust boundary. sessionCredentialFromConsole: true is the pivot field separating console-sourced sessions from programmatic access.

item.title: Incident response guide for AWS CloudTrail investigations – Part 2
item.description:
SSRF to IMDSv1 credential theft cascades into multi-Region Amazon Bedrock misuse. AWS SIRT breaks down the full attack chain with annotated CloudTrail evidence and a response checklist.
Key findings:
- The chain started with an SSRF flaw in a web app on an EC2 instance carrying the "webdev" IAM role. Because IMDSv1 requires no session token, the attacker hit 169.254.169.254 and walked away with temporary role credentials. The CloudTrail smoking gun is ec2RoleDelivery: "1.0" in the userIdentity block. That single field confirms IMDSv1 delivery and the SSRF vector without needing application logs.
- Four events tell the whole story: a failed CreateUser for "adm1n" (typosquatting with a numeral 1) at 15:53 UTC, a no-MFA ConsoleLogin success at 15:59, a ListFoundationModels recon call in us-east-2 at 17:20, then a Converse invocation of amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 at 17:25. Same source IP 75.3.231[.]105, same webdev role session throughout.
- The Region hop from us-east-1 to us-east-2 was deliberate evasion. Inconsistent cross-Region monitoring let the Bedrock activity go initially unnoticed. sessionCredentialFromConsole: "true" in Event 3 ties the Bedrock calls back to the hijacked console session, not a fresh credential pull.
- CloudTrail records the Converse call and token counts (944 input, 126 output) but NOT prompt or response content. If Bedrock model invocation logging was not enabled, the data sent to the model cannot be recovered post-incident.

item.title: Attackers Actively Exploiting Critical Vulnerability in Super Forms Plugin
item.description:
CVE-2026-14894 (CVSS 9.8): Unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Super Forms WordPress plugin is actively exploited at scale, with 250,000+ blocked attempts and PHP webshells being dropped on vulnerable sites.
- CVE-2026-14894 affects Super Forms <= 6.3.313. The submit_form() nopriv AJAX handler accepts a base64-encoded datauristring, decodes it, and writes it to disk using an attacker-controlled filename with zero file-type validation. A valid nonce is freely minted via the super_create_nonce nopriv endpoint, so the full exploit chain is just two unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php.
- The webshell observed in the wild is named Mushr00w_upl.php, a browser-based uploader used to stage further payloads. Exploitation began July 14, 2026, five days after disclosure, with a major spike August 18-25. Top offending IPs include 103.168.147[.]235 (106k+ requests) and 103.168.146[.]131 (82k+ requests).
- For incident response: search the entire WordPress docroot for .php files created or modified on or after July 8, 2026. Check web server access logs for POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=super_submit_form. The filename Mushr00w_upl.php is a strong IOC but attackers vary filenames and can use path traversal to place shells outside the upload directory.
Patch to Super Forms 6.3.314 immediately.

item.title: Modern Adventures in Azure Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The "Anyscale Platform Administrator Role" Azure built-in role allowed unconstrained escalation to Owner-equivalent access, reported to MSRC 6/8/2026 and patched 6/22/2026.
- The Anyscale Platform Administrator Role (GUID 3e9f3756-203e-4734-a0b8-4b68691ffae3) held Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write and /delete without any ABAC Conditions. Of 28 built-in roles carrying roleAssignments/write, only 4 lacked constraining ABAC Conditions: Owner, User Access Administrator, RBAC Administrator, and this role. Any principal holding it could arbitrarily assign any role, including Owner, to any principal in scope.
- The recommended Azure Portal ABAC Condition ("Allow user to assign all roles except Owner, UAA, RBAC") can be bypassed because it constrains only roleAssignments/write and /delete, not Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/write. A constrained Owner or UAA can create a custom role with * or roleAssignments/write, then self-assign it, and the unconstrained custom role takes priority.
- The undocumented ARM API endpoint (Role Definitions List, version 2023-07-01-preview) with the hasAllPermissions filter lets you map any permission directly to every built-in and custom role that contains it, surfacing unexpected hits like Log Analytics Contributor and Virtual Machine Contributor both holding Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action.

item.title: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
An AI-era evasion technique jumped from prompt injection research into high-volume phishing: invisible Unicode tag characters (U+E0000-U+E007F) spliced into financial keywords to break spam filters, peaking at 2.37 million messages per day.
Key findings:
- Starting February 9, 2026, signature hits jumped from ~21,000 to 1.3 million messages overnight. The campaign ran weekdays only, paused every weekend, peaked February 26, and dropped sharply after May 15. Finance-themed lure words like "funding" were split as fun[U+E0020]ding, defeating literal string matches and disrupting ML tokenizers without alerting recipients. MITRE T1027 / AML.T0068.
- ~150 disposable sender domains built from a recycled 28-token finance vocabulary (capital, fund, loan, loc, boost, etc.) relayed through ActiveCampaign infrastructure. Envelope senders follow the pattern em-[digits].[brand-domain]; click-tracking routes through acemlnd[.]com and activehosted[.]com. ~92% of volume originated from 173.236.20[.]0/24, a legitimate shared platform block useful for scoping, not blocking alone.
- The detection gap: pipelines that do not normalize U+E0000-U+E007F before applying signatures or ML classifiers may miss the obfuscation. OCR-based content analysis sidesteps it entirely. Exclude England/Scotland/Wales flag emojis (legitimately encoded with tag characters) before treating the range as malicious.

item.title: From ClickFix to SilentEncryptor: A Simple Yet Destructive Path to Ransomware Deployment
item.description:
StopAndProtect campaign uses ClickFix social engineering on hacked WordPress sites to deploy SilentEncryptor ransomware, active since May 2026 with 22 confirmed variants now identified.
- ClickFix is the initial access vector (T1204.002): visitors to compromised WordPress sites see a fake CAPTCHA prompt that instructs them to copy and run a PowerShell command, handing the attacker execution without any exploit.
- SilentEncryptor pulls its target list and ransom note dynamically from C2, meaning the attacker controls which endpoints get encrypted and can rotate messaging between victims. Three original samples share the embedded marker string "*V*RrETTY" and base64-encoded wallet paths covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, Exodus, Dash, Dogecoin, and others under AppData\Roaming.
- A suspected OPSEC failure caused the threat actor to upload their own desktop files to C2, giving researchers rare visibility into the operation's infrastructure, all hosted on the same pool of vulnerable WordPress sites.
- Stairwell's YARA rule scanned their malware corpus and surfaced 22 variants beyond the original three, with sample hashes including 65550f6d0ffec8421f703cdc7273d9c0563b3d480fe6702bad294a18afe72143 and a5b512c09a6b0add18397238d0c64ff34b6d95f4114efe808df03e3e11c29fb1.
Deploy the YARA rule retroactively across your environment and hunt for PowerShell processes spawned from browser or clipboard activity. Full IOC list and YARA rule are in the report.

item.title: AI-Generated BEC Phishing from a Compromised Mailbox | Invictus Incident Response
item.description:
AI-polished BEC arrives from a legitimately compromised mailbox, bypassing reputation filters. A two-stage redirect chain (AWS S3 to Cloudflare-fronted domain) ends in an AiTM Google credential harvester.
Key findings:
- The lure originated from a real grocery retailer's compromised mailbox, subject "Urgent Review Required - Purchase Order and Invoice Discrepancies." No lookalike domain, no spoof signal for gateways to catch. Body assessed as LLM-generated: structurally flawless, generically polite, missing the specific PO numbers a real dispute would include (T1199, T1078.004).
- Redirect chain: projectorg878990.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws[.]com/index.html poses as an "RFP Access Portal," then bounces to purchasesord[.]com (Cloudflare-fronted, first seen 25 Aug 2026), which serves a Google sign-in page using socket.io to relay credentials and session tokens to the actor (T1557, T1583.006).
- The kit exposed itself: a code comment references swapping in a grant endpoint, and the badge reads "Community Charter School." A school/grant phishing kit was repurposed for a financial lure with placeholders left in, the branding never matched the sender.
- Pivoting surfaced related low-confidence infrastructure: accessdocuments[.]us, accountsv3slgnin-identifier-continue[.]com, adobeonlinereader[.]org, docsngdocumm[.]com, getmailsg[.]com, securepreesserrve[.]com, yah-signrev[.]info.
On a suspected BEC: suspend active sessions and tokens, not just the password.

item.title: Contagious Interview steps outside the developer workflow
item.description:
DPRK Contagious Interview expands beyond developer bait: 14 trojanized macOS apps impersonating tools like The Unarchiver, Sketch, and Bartender deliver OtterCookie via a four-stage chain.
Key findings:
- Unsigned DMGs and PKGs impersonate popular Mac apps. CFBundleExecutable in Info.plist is hijacked to point to a hidden .macos file compiled via Bunster (shell-to-Go). Gatekeeper blocks execution, so the quarantine xattr must be manually stripped, suggesting targeted delivery where victims are coached through the bypass.
- The four-stage chain: .macos curls /task/mac from 162.0.239[.]85, which fetches tokenlinux.sh, which pulls Node.js and a malicious parser.js. Staging now uses the hidden ~/.task directory. Every retrieval URL beyond the first carries a signed HS256 JWT embedding victim IP, sessionId, step counter, and timestamps.
- Final payload is OtterCookie: a Socket.IO RAT, browser and crypto wallet credential stealer, in-memory filesystem scanner, and clipboard clipper using pbpaste.
- Infrastructure: staging on 162.0.239[.]85:3000, OtterCookie C2 on 147.124.202[.]205 across ports 7671, 7676, 7679. Associated domains include w3pi[.]social, softcus[.]net, and pobelstudio[.]com.
Hunt for unsigned apps with modified Info.plist executables, outbound HTTP to port 3000, Node.js spawned from unexpected parents, and ~/.task directory creation.

item.title: One Blank Field Bypasses Direct Send Control
item.description:
A single empty SMTP envelope field bypasses RejectDirectSend in Microsoft 365, letting unauthenticated senders spoof internal addresses with no credentials, no lookalike domain, and no infrastructure.
- RejectDirectSend evaluates the domain in the SMTP MAIL FROM field, but an empty value (MAIL FROM:<>) gives it nothing to check. ReliaQuest confirmed this in a controlled tenant: the baseline message with an accepted-domain envelope sender was rejected with 550 5.7.68, while the empty-sender message was accepted and queued, headers showing spf=none, dkim=none, dmarc=fail action=oreject, SCL 9, and delivery to Junk. Junk delivery is not a win: the bypass already succeeded before antispam ran.
- Active phishing use from September 2025 through August 2026 across multiple orgs, targeting executives, finance, and procurement with file-sharing and payment lures, several using SVG attachments framed as voicemails. Most messages reached inboxes via filtering exceptions on impersonated addresses, not inbox placement by default.
- IP-restricted inbound connectors blocked every Direct Send attempt regardless of envelope sender in testing. This is the structural fix. RejectDirectSend alone is not sufficient.
Hunt for messages where the envelope Return-Path is empty and the header From uses an accepted internal domain, cross-reference against SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures and any override that let them deliver.

item.title: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence exposes a hands-on-keyboard campaign abusing Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT helpdesk, deploy a Node.js backdoor, and pivot to domain controllers via WinRM.
- Initial access (T1566.003) starts with an external Teams chat or vishing call from a threat-actor-controlled tenant. The actor socially engineers the user into launching Quick Assist or another RMM tool and reading back the session code, bypassing Teams' external-contact warnings through urgency and pretext ("Microsoft Security Update," account deactivation threats). The remote-assist process tree spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell immediately after is the first detectable signal.
- PowerShell downloads a masqueraded MSI ("devfix," "Hotfix") from Azure Blob Storage endpoints including update1n5[.]blob.core.windows[.]net through update1n9[.]blob.core.windows[.]net and installs it silently via msiexec /qn (T1218.007). The MSI drops an encrypted implant and a portable Node.js runtime into LocalAppData, persisting via an HKCU Run value or Startup folder shortcut named EdgeUpdate.
- The Node.js implant (Trojan:JS/EtherRatz.A!MTB, B!MTB) polls C2 via randomized HTTPS long-polling to synctimes.australiaeast.cloudapp.azure[.]com. It executes operator-delivered JavaScript tasks: ADSI enumeration of domain servers and user descriptions, Base64-encoded screen captures written to temp files, and rundll32-loaded second-stage DLLs (T1218.011).

item.title: How Attackers Learn Your Network Before They Attack It
item.description:
Zeek's bro-simple-scan exposes how failed TCP connections betray reconnaissance, and why encoding network knowledge beats pure threshold counting for catching patient adversaries.
- bro-simple-scan watches Zeek connection history strings, S (SYN with no response) and Sr (SYN plus RST), counting unique victim/port pairs per source. At 25 failures it fires one of three notices: Scan::Address_Scan (one source, many hosts), Scan::Port_Scan (one source, one host, many ports), or Scan::Random_Scan (scattered pattern). Darknet integration via bro-is-darknet drops the threshold to 10 when a source touches unused address space, and a separate knock-knock rule fires at 20 unique hosts on a single port (3 if darknet).
- The structural blind spot is slow and distributed scanning. State ages out after 15 minutes by default, so a scanner pacing below two probes per half hour never accumulates enough failures. Split across 50 sources, no single source trips a per-source threshold even when the aggregate pattern is obvious.
- Profile-based detection is the upgrade path. A SYN to a port no host in your network legitimately serves is high-confidence at count one. Zeek already logs every connection; building a baseline of which hosts serve which ports, and who talks to whom, inverts the detection question from "has this source failed enough?" to "does this connection make sense?"

item.title: CVE-2026-81578: Exploited PaperCut Authentication Bypass Chains to Pre-Auth RCE
item.description:
CVE-2026-81578 (CVSS 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 are actively exploited zero-days in PaperCut NG/MF, chaining an auth bypass to unsafe Java class loading for pre-auth RCE as SYSTEM. Both are in CISA KEV; federal remediation deadline is September 14, 2026.
- CVE-2026-81578 lets an unauthenticated attacker craft a request that references one page for rendering while targeting a different backend component, causing PaperCut to validate the wrong page and skip access control. This alone allows unauthorized config changes. Chained with CVE-2026-82078, which loads Java driver classes from a configurable name without an allowlist, an attacker writes attacker-controlled config then triggers arbitrary Java bytecode execution. Huntress confirmed charmap.exe ran as SYSTEM under pc-app.exe on PaperCut NG 25.0.11.75758. A public PoC exists.
- First exploitation observed August 26, 2026. Attackers ran whoami, ver, tasklist, nltest, and quser from the PaperCut process tree, dropped malicious .class files (lib/Udydn.class), then installed SimpleHelp as a persistent service named "Remote Access Service" under LocalSystem, and fetched AnyDesk.

item.title: Chamilo LMS... It's raining 0days, hallelujah, it's raining 0days
item.description:
Chamilo LMS 1.11.36 has 11 zero-days including a fully weaponized pre-auth RCE chain. Schools and enterprises running this widely deployed open-source LMS are exposed to complete server compromise with no credentials required.
Key findings:
- The pre-auth RCE chain starts with CVE-2026-61600, an unauthenticated boolean-based blind SQLi in main/inc/ajax/model.ajax.php via the groupOp field of the JSON filters parameter. An attacker needs only a valid cidReq course code (enumerable from the home page) to dump the admin row including the confirmation_token field, enabling a full password reset without ever touching the admin's mailbox.
- A second pre-auth primitive (no CVE assigned separately) allows unauthenticated POST requests to main/inc/ajax/user_manager.ajax.php with action update_users, overwriting the email of any user including admin (user_id=1). Chained with the password reset flow this gives complete account takeover. The admin row can be restored post-exploit to minimize detection.
- CVE-2026-70647 is an unsafe deserialization in the course backup import feature. course_info.dat inside the ZIP is base64-encoded serialized PHP. An attacker modifies a Document object's path property to coiffeur.php in the web root, re-packages the ZIP, and imports it via the legitimate course import UI. Chamilo trusts the tampered metadata and writes the webshell to /app/courses/{course_code}/coiffeur.php.

item.title: Attackers Actively Exploiting Critical Vulnerability in Elementor Pro Plugin
item.description:
CVE-2026-32475 (CVSS 9.8) in Elementor Pro is actively exploited, letting unauthenticated attackers upload PHP webshells and take over any WordPress site running the vulnerable plugin across 6 million active installs.
- CVE-2026-32475 hits Elementor Pro <= 4.2.1 via a validation logic flaw in Upload::validation(). Submitting a file upload field as an array where index [0] has an empty filename triggers UPLOAD_ERR_NO_FILE, which causes a premature 'return' instead of 'continue', killing all extension and MIME checks for every subsequent array element. Index [1] then delivers a .php webshell unchallenged, no authentication required.
- The dropped file lands in wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/ under a randomized name with the attacker-supplied .php extension. That directory should never contain PHP files: its presence is your primary IOC. The webshell observed chains system, passthru, shell_exec, exec, proc_open, and popen for maximum exec compatibility.
- Exploitation began the same day of public disclosure, August 19th, 2026. Over 190,000 attempts blocked. Top attacking IPs include 185.196.220[.]85, 103.84.230[.]85, 103.90.148[.]202, and 216.126.225[.]208.
Hunt your access logs for POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=elementor_pro_forms_send_form, then scan wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/ for any .php file. Patch to 4.2.2 immediately.

item.title: Gaming the system: how a Chinese-speaking actor turned Brazilian government sites into an SEO weapon
item.description:
Gambling Goblin, a Chinese-speaking cluster linked to Earth Berberoka, has compromised Brazilian 🇧🇷 government .gov.br servers since mid-2025, weaponizing their search reputation for gambling SEO fraud while deploying espionage-grade Linux tooling.

item.description:

Untappd for Android leaves behind SQLite databases, compressed API cache, and push notification XML that together reconstruct a user's location history, identity, and check-in timeline.
Key findings:
- Two SQLite databases may exist under data/data/com.untappdllc.app/databases: clevertap (table: userProfiles, column: data) holds name, username, email, gender, date of birth as Unix seconds, and last checked-in beer. superwall_database (table: ManagedEventData) logs app_install, app_launch, app_close, and device_attributes events with epoch timestamps in milliseconds, approximate IP-derived location, OS version, app version, and network type.
- The cache folder at data/data/com.untappdllc.app/cache/http-cache stores gzip-compressed JSON files. Files with a .1 extension contain API responses including Discover page GPS coordinates, full check-in records with timestamps, beer and venue details, and Foursquare location suggestions. The paired .0 metadata file provides the timestamp when coordinates were loaded, filling the gap where the JSON itself carries no time value.
- Push notifications are preserved in shared_prefs/io.invertase.firebase.xml as JSON entries containing title, body, pushType, and a messageId embedding a Unix epoch timestamp. This can surface venue alerts, beer stock notifications, and social interactions even after the app UI is cleared.

item.title: Password spraying campaign targets AWS root user accounts across 150+ organizations
item.description:
Password spraying campaign hit AWS root accounts at 150+ organizations between July 24 and August 23, 2026, with attackers rotating residential proxies and outdated browser user agents to mask the activity.
Key findings:
- The campaign generated ConsoleLogin failures logged under userIdentity.type:Root in CloudTrail. A failed root ConsoleLogin only fires when the attacker supplies a valid root email address, meaning they arrived with a pre-built list or enumerated addresses first. Median hit rate was 2 attempts per org, up to 8.
- Two static user agents fingerprint every request: a Chrome 85/Edge 85 string and a Firefox 120 string. These are stale versions, an easy hunt pivot. All source IPs resolve to hosting infrastructure or residential proxies across mixed ASNs and countries.
- AWS mandated MFA for root users as of June 2025, but a 35-day grace window between first sign-in and MFA registration exists. No successful authentication was observed, but the attacker intent remains unknown.
- The additionalEventData block in the CloudTrail record shows MFAUsed:No and a billing console redirect, suggesting the spray targeted the management console login path directly.
Takeaway: Query CloudTrail now for ConsoleLogin events where userIdentity.type is Root and userAgent matches either fingerprint above. Alert on any root sign-in, successful or failed.

item.title: Breaking the Seal: Static Deobfuscation of JSCeal’s Compiled V8 Bytecode
item.description:
JSCeal crypto-stealer hides inside compiled V8 bytecode. Check Point Research built a fully static deobfuscation pipeline to crack it open without executing the malware, exposing keylogging, browser credential theft, and an HTTPS MITM proxy.
- JSCeal (also tagged WEEVILPROXY or MeadowLocust) arrives as app.jsc, a Brotli-compressed V8 code cache executed by a bundled Node.js runtime. The delivery chain starts with malvertising, drops multiple PowerShell stages, and unpacks two ZIPs: node.zip (the runtime) and build.zip (the payload plus winpty-agent.exe, winpty.dll, and preflight.js). Because the JavaScript was obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator before V8 compilation, analysts receive RC4-encrypted string chunks, control-flow flattening, proxy indirection, and operation wrappers on top of version-sensitive bytecode.
- Check Point's open-source jsc_deobfuscator pipeline (github.com/hasherezade/jsc_deobfuscator) layers: Brotli decompression, V8 disassembly (patched for the exact Node.js V8 10.2.154.26-node.25 build), View8 decompilation with pickle serialization, then ordered passes: value propagation, RC4 string reconstruction (~130k encoded chunks per sample), control-flow unflattening, proxy/operation resolution. An optional LLM renaming stage (Claude or GPT) labels the resulting function graph. All 23 collected payloads produced analyzable output.

item.title: A KQL Query Is Not a Detection: What My Microsoft Sentinel Lab Actually Validated
item.description:
A compiled KQL query is not proof of detection: this Sentinel lab shows the full validation chain from raw telemetry through alert and incident, and reveals which rules earned that status.
- Telemetry routing is the foundation. AzureActivity requires an explicit subscription diagnostic setting (activity-to-sentinelsiem). AuditLogs and AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs each need their own Entra diagnostic setting routed to the workspace. Neither arrives by default, and a daily cap gap is not evidence of no activity.
- Rule 1 (AuditLogs, app/SP credential change) is event-match validated: the lab observed the exact ActivityDisplayName values "Add application", "Add service principal", "Add service principal credentials", and "Update application - Certificates and secrets management" and confirmed the KQL returns them. Full validation still requires SecurityAlert and SecurityIncident rows confirmed via the SecurityIncident table query.
- Rule 2 (AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs, same SessionId across 2+ IPs, T1550.001) and Rule 3 (cross-table join correlating auth then directory change within 30 min, T1098.001) remain disabled and unvalidated because the lab could not reproduce the exact trigger conditions in both native tables.
- The honest validation chain is: test action, raw telemetry row, KQL result, SecurityAlert, SecurityIncident. Stopping at KQL row match overstates confidence.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: Dark Caracal Deploys New Go Malware With Ethereum-Based C2 Fallback
item.description:
Lebanese APT Dark Caracal deploys GoCaracal, a new Go-based framework with an Ethereum smart-contract C2 fallback, alongside an updated Bandook backdoor targeting Venezuela.
- Phishing emails with tax/financial lures deliver weaponised SVG attachments that redirect through URL shorteners to getpdfdigital[.]cloud, staging a 7-Zip archive containing the lightweight GoCaracal implant. The SVG-as-delivery-vehicle is a detection gap: many mail filters pass SVGs without content inspection.
- GoCaracal runs two profiles. The lightweight build handles host profiling, encrypted C2, remote shell, and shellcode injection. The extended build adds keylogging, browser credential and cookie theft, WebRTC remote desktop, SOCKS5 proxy, and a Ethereum smart-contract fallback using a custom Solidity contract named BulletproofC2, letting operators swap the C2 address on-chain without redeploying the implant.
- 23 of 24 GoCaracal C2 addresses sit on AEZA Group networks; Bandook C2s are hosted on AlexHost. That deliberate provider split compartmentalises infrastructure and limits takedown blast radius.
- The updated Bandook sample replaced sequential command IDs (@0001-@0136) with randomised strings and obfuscated plugin export names, deliberately breaking older signature-based detections.
Hunt: block or alert on SVG files in email, flag outbound JSON-RPC calls to public Ethereum endpoints (eth_call pattern), and scan for Go binaries connecting to AEZA-hosted IPs.

item.title: Wordfence Argus Finds Critical Authentication Bypass in WPMU DEV Dashboard Plugin
item.description:
CVE-2026-76581 (CVSS 9.8): Unauthenticated auth bypass in WPMU DEV Dashboard lets attackers claim an admin session on ~350,000 WordPress sites via HMAC canonicalization confusion in the Hub SSO flow. Patch to 5.0.2 now.
Key findings:
- CVE-2026-76581, CVSS 9.8 Critical. Affects WPMU DEV Dashboard versions up to and including 5.0.1 on sites with Hub SSO enabled and mapped to an administrator. Exploitation is unauthenticated and leads to full site takeover, and to RCE if the plugin or theme editor is accessible.
- The root cause is HMAC canonicalization confusion between the two AJAX actions wdpsso_step1 and wdpsso_step2, both exposed to unauthenticated visitors. Step 1 signs token||state||redirect||domain without delimiters. Step 2 verifies token||state||redirect, omitting domain. An attacker calls step 1 with an empty redirect, receives a valid HMAC over token||state||domain, then replays it to step 2 with domain moved into the redirect field. The byte strings are identical so verification passes. Step 1 acts as a signing oracle.
- The patch stores the step-1 HMAC server-side and explicitly rejects any step-2 submission where the incoming HMAC matches the stored step-1 value, breaking the replay.
- Wordfence Premium, Care, and Response customers received a firewall rule August 25. Free users receive it September 24. Sites that cannot update immediately should disable Hub SSO.
Update to 5.0.2 immediately.

item.title: Inside 90 days of attacks on AI infrastructure
item.description:
90 days of honeypot telemetry expose three active attack patterns against AI infrastructure: RCE via MCP server flaws, blind prompt injection against agent frameworks, and AI-native post-exploitation targeting model API keys in memory.
- Two CVEs in LiteLLM are being actively exploited. CVE-2026-59822 is an OAuth2 bypass where a single-character Bearer token (Bearer x) grants full MCP gateway access. CVE-2026-42271, added to CISA KEV in June 2026, is a command injection in MCP test endpoints where the command field hits subprocess with no validation. Attackers used it to deploy the gmon cryptominer, running detached via start_new_session=True with the staging directory wiped post-launch, leaving little on disk. These two chain with a Starlette host header bypass (CVE-2026-48710) for unauthenticated RCE. The Qilin ransomware group has been linked to that chain.
- Blind prompt injection hit LangChain, Flowise, OpenWebUI, and Node-RED. Attackers injected instruction-override prompts that triggered shell tool execution and fired DNS callbacks to attacker-controlled OAST domains for out-of-band confirmation, keeping the payload out of app logs. XMRig was staged at /usr/src/node-red/xmrig to blend with the Node.js process tree.
- Post-exploitation is AI-native. On LiteLLM, attackers queried Python module state in memory to extract the master key rather than hunting disk files.

item.title: Cleartext Credential Recovery in ServiceNow
item.description:
Attackers with ServiceNow discovery_admin rights can backdoor the CredentialTestAjax script include to dump cleartext secrets, including SSH keys, Entra ID service principal secrets, and AWS keys, from the discovery_credentials table.
Key details:
- The technique targets the CredentialTestAjax script include via a POST to /xmlhttp.do. Inserting an early return before the SNC.CredentialTest.test() call forces the server to return the decrypted JSON blob to the client, bypassing the UI restriction that hides raw secrets even from admins. Works for all 27 discovery credential types, not just Windows accounts.
- Requires discovery_admin (or agent_admin plus script_include_admin), which also grants read access to discovery_credentials via sys_id lookup. discovery_admin bundles script_include_admin by default, so one overprivileged account unlocks the full chain.
- LDAP credentials stored in ldap_server_config use the Password2 field type. A separately created script include calling getDecryptedValue() recovers cleartext LDAP bind passwords and requires only script_include_admin, fewer rights than the existing forced-auth LDAP technique.
- Forensic pivot: review the sys_script_include audit log for recent modifications to CredentialTestAjax or any newly created script includes. Correlate with /xmlhttp.do AJAX calls in HTTP access logs around the same timestamps.

item.title: Version Control DFIR: a Cheatsheet to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps
item.description:
Version Control Systems are under-logged and under-prepared: Wiz CIRT releases a DFIR cheatsheet mapping audit events, log gaps, and ATT&CK-aligned detections across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.
Key findings:
- Log retention defaults create blind spots that cost investigators scope. GitHub retains Git read/write events for only 7 days by default. GitLab does not write Git operations to the database at all without pre-configured log streaming. In a real Wiz CIRT case, missing historical git.clone events meant the full scope of exfiltrated repos could not be determined, forcing a broad credential rotation across the entire org instead of a precise, targeted response.
- API logs are nearly invisible across SaaS VCS platforms. GitHub is currently the only hosted provider that allows organizations to capture raw API requests, and doing so requires explicit configuration and streaming. These logs are critical for detecting early-stage enumeration before any impact occurs.
- The ATT&CK-aligned forensic matrix maps the same attacker behavior to different event names per platform. Mass repo cloning appears as git.clone on GitHub, repository_git_operation on GitLab, and RepositoryCloneEvent on Bitbucket Data Center. Knowing the right event name before an incident is the difference between a targeted query and a blind hunt.

item.title: Hunting Abuse: Detecting Privilege Escalation Through the ADCS Database
item.description:
The ADCS CA database is an underused forensic goldmine: it logs every certificate request including denied ones, exposing ESC1 privilege escalation attempts without any extra logging configuration.
Key findings:
- The CA database at C:\Windows\System32\CertLog\ is an ESE file that records all requests across four tables: Requests, Certificates, RequestAttributes, and inline request text. Denied requests are preserved permanently, meaning an attacker who tried and failed to impersonate a privileged identity via a misconfigured template still leaves a record including the UPN they specified as the Subject Alternative Name.
- CISA Advisory AA26-237A (August 2026) confirms ESC1 was used in red team assessments to compromise domains. ESC1 lets any domain user request a certificate for any other user when templates allow enrollee-supplied subjects and permit Client Authentication, producing a valid TGT for the impersonated account.
- A bug in the go-ese library caused all DateTime columns in the ADCS database to return 1899-12-30T00:00:00Z because Flags=0 columns were decoded as OLE doubles instead of Windows FILETIMEs. The fix, now merged and shipping in Velociraptor 0.76.6+, inspects the float value itself to select the correct decoder.
- Velociraptor reads the locked CA database via its raw NTFS accessor and replays the ESE transaction log, requiring zero changes to CA config, no agents, and no Windows Event Log dependency.

item.title: JavaScript obfuscation: From party trick to phishing kit
item.description:
Cisco Talos breaks down JavaScript obfuscation tradecraft used in phishing kits and malware loaders, with a practitioner workflow for turning hidden behavior into observable behavior.
Key details:
- Obfuscation techniques stack: string splitting, hex/Unicode/Base64 encoding, lookup tables with _0x-prefixed identifiers, dynamic property access (window["doc"+"ument"]), control-flow flattening into state machines, JSFuck punctuation soup, and dead-code noise. These hide URLs, exfil endpoints, and API calls from static search. Beautifying helps readability but restores none of this.
- Runtime code generation is the critical choke point. eval(), Function(), and setTimeout("") all act as execution sinks. The practical move: replace the sink with console.log(), capture the intermediate payload, and analyze that layer separately in isolation.
- npm package scripts extend the threat beyond the browser. preinstall/postinstall hooks running obfuscated Node.js can reach process.env, SSH keys, npm tokens, GitHub tokens, CI secrets, and the filesystem. "What does it read?" no longer means cookies; it means build-runner secrets.
- Anti-analysis tricks include debugger loops, DevTools-open detection, timing-based breakpoint detection, navigator.webdriver checks, domain locks, and console.log replacement. The goal is not permanence; it is outlasting the first five minutes of analysis.

item.title: CISA Red Team Fully Compromised Two Critical Infrastructure Orgs
item.description:
CISA red team fully compromised two critical infrastructure orgs via default creds, ESC1, and DCSync. One SOC detected and contained in minutes; the other never knew until CISA debriefed them.
Key findings:
- Organization A (Government Facilities) fell to a default-credential web app used to send internal phishing, then ESC1 abuse in AD Certificate Services let a low-priv user request admin certs. The red team reached all targeted systems, pivoted to cloud, and read SOC emails to confirm no detection. Multiple siloed SOCs with different EDR solutions and no cross-team visibility meant a real SCCM alert was marked false positive and never escalated.
- Organization B (Water/Wastewater) caught the initial compromise fast and forced an assume-breach posture, but still had critical gaps: a plaintext password in an XML file on an SCCM share, leading to DCSync and krbtgt hash extraction, enabling Golden Tickets. RDP files on a jump server exposed an OT-adjacent bastion reachable via FTP creds and SSH.
- Both orgs lacked Conditional Access for workload identities, letting the red team abuse Microsoft Graph API permissions to read tenant-wide email. Org A also had non-expiring AWS IAM keys sitting in user home directories.
Treat SCCM as Tier 0. Audit ADCS templates for CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT. Hunt cleartext creds on shares. Enable Conditional Access for workload identities now. Full ATT&CK mapping is in advisory AA26-237A.
